title: Smooth formal matter, EM tensors and observer quantities

items.title: Smooth formal matter, EM tensors and observer quantities
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

items.title: Charged dust balance equivalence and advected charge ratio
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian domain of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $ho,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$ with $ho>0$, and let $U\in C^2(\Omega,T\Omega)$ be future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Set $T_m^{ab}=ho U^aU^b$, $j^a=\sigma U^a$, and $a^b=U^a
abla_aU^b$. Assume the formal matter-exchange equation $
abla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. Then this equation is equivalent on $\Omega$ to

$$
abla_a(ho U^a)=0,\qquad ho a^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c.$$

On $\Omega$, define $\alpha=\sigma/ho$. Under the continuity equation, charge-current conservation $
abla_aj^a=0$ is equivalent to $U^a
abla_a\alpha=0$. Thus the equation constrains the derivative of $\alpha$ along the dust flow; it does not impose spatial constancy of $\alpha$. The claim is a pointwise conditional identity and supplies no coupled-field existence theorem or Maxwell equation.

items.title: Perfect-fluid exchange projections and conduction heating
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $\epsilon,p,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$ and let $U\in C^2(\Omega,T\Omega)$ be future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Set

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},\qquad a^b=U^a\nabla_aU^b,\quad D=U^a\nabla_a,\quad \theta=\nabla_aU^a,\quad h^b{}_c=\delta^b{}_c+\frac{U^bU_c}{c^2}.$$

For a current $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$, define $f^b=F^b{}_cj^c$ and assume the mathematical exchange equation $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=f^b$. Then it is equivalent to the longitudinal and rest-space equations

$$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\theta=-U_bf^b,\qquad \frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}a^b+h^{ba}\nabla_ap=h^b{}_cf^c.$$

The rest electric field of $U$ is $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$. If $q^a=\chi E_U^a$ for a specified scalar $\chi\ge0$, then the electromagnetic contribution to the comoving energy balance is $-U_bf^b=\chi\,g(E_U,E_U)\ge0$. For $q=0$ it is zero. The Ohmic relation is an additional constitutive hypothesis; no equation of state, entropy law, or fluid existence result follows.

items.title: Pointwise Maxwell and matter energy-condition vocabulary
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, metric $g$, and future cone of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Here timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, null means $v\ne0$ and $g(v,v)=0$, causal means timelike or null, and a nonzero causal vector is future-directed when $g(v,N)<0$, as in that supplier. A future unit observer is a vector $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$. At a point $p$, let $T_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous real symmetric bilinear form, represented by the covariant tensor $T_{ab}$. Define its metric trace by $\operatorname{tr}_g T:=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ and its raised mixed tensor by $T^a{}_b:=g^{ac}T_{cb}$.

- The **weak energy condition (WEC)** holds at $p$ when $T_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v\in T_pM$.
- The **null energy condition (NEC)** holds at $p$ when $T_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future-directed null $\ell\in T_pM$.
- The **strong energy condition (SEC)** holds at $p$ when the WEC holds for the trace-reversed tensor $T_{ab}-\tfrac12(\operatorname{tr}_gT)g_{ab}$.
- The **dominant energy condition (DEC)** holds at $p$ when, for every future-directed timelike $v\in T_pM$, the vector $J^a:=-T^a{}_bv^b$ is future causal or zero.

These are pointwise algebraic conditions. They are independent of an Einstein equation or an assertion that a physical material realizes $T$. The continuous regularity suffices for the definitions; any differentiability needed for a conservation identity is a separate hypothesis.

For a future unit observer $n$, observer energy density means $T_{ab}n^an^b$. The observer energy-current vector is $-T^a{}_bn^b$, and its spatial energy flux is the projection of this vector into the positive rest space $n^\perp$.

items.title: EM, dust and perfect-fluid energy inequalities
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Use the energy-condition definitions of [[def-emg-pointwise-energy-conditions]] and the matter and Maxwell tensor definitions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. At every point of an oriented time-oriented Lorentzian domain, the Maxwell tensor $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ of that definition is symmetric, trace-free, and satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC. Its observer energy density and energy flux in a positively oriented orthonormal rest frame are

$$u=\frac{|E|^2/c^2+|B|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad \frac{E\times B}{\mu_0c},$$

and the DEC flux is future causal or zero. A charged-dust tensor with $\rho\ge0$ satisfies all four conditions. For a perfect-fluid tensor with rest energy density $\epsilon$ and pressure $p$, the exact pointwise conditions are

$$\mathrm{WEC}\iff \epsilon\ge0\text{ and }\epsilon+p\ge0,\quad \mathrm{NEC}\iff\epsilon+p\ge0,$$

$$\mathrm{SEC}\iff\epsilon+p\ge0\text{ and }\epsilon+3p\ge0,\quad \mathrm{DEC}\iff\epsilon\ge|p|.$$

At a point, finite sums of tensors satisfying any one of these conditions still satisfy that condition; in particular $T_{\mathrm{EM}}+T_m$ satisfies all four for nonnegative dust. No general matter positivity assumption is made, and adding $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ to an arbitrary fluid need not repair a violated fluid inequality.

items.title: Covariant acceleration along a $C^2$ curve
items.design_state: Complete locally authored definition or conditional proof with all stated hypotheses and explicit dependencies.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with an affine connection $\nabla$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be any interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]), and let $z:I\to M$ be $C^2$ in the sense of clause (a) of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]: in each curve chart the first and second coordinate derivatives extend continuously to every included endpoint, where derivatives are one-sided. Put $U(\tau):=z'(\tau)$, using the one-sided derivative at included endpoints. A continuous vector field along $z$ means an assignment $V(\tau)\in T_{z(\tau)}M$ whose component functions are continuous in every local chart. In a chart $x=(x^a)$ covering a segment of $z$, write $U^a(\tau):=\frac{d}{d\tau}(x^a\circ z)(\tau)$ and let $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$. Define the **covariant acceleration of $z$** on this segment by the component formula

$$\bigl(\nabla_UU\bigr)^a(\tau):=\frac{dU^a}{d\tau}(\tau)+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(z(\tau))U^b(\tau)U^c(\tau).$$

The $C^2$ regularity makes $U^a$ continuously differentiable, including one-sided endpoint derivatives, so these components are continuous on the relative parameter interval. The name and notation extend the pullback covariant derivative of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] from smooth curves; the coordinate expression is well-defined on overlaps by [[lem-emg-c2-curve-covariant-acceleration-well-defined]].

items.title: Killing exchange current and gauge-compensated charged first integral
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof authored. The current Maxwell-stress supplier is a draft with escalated readiness through its action-variation and batch-2 local-potential proof chain; this result remains explicitly conditional and escalated.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an oriented open subset of the time-oriented Lorentzian domain of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $F$ and $j$ be smooth, let $T_m^{ab}$ be smooth and symmetric, and suppose

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad \nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c.$$

Let $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the tensor of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]] and assume the exact conditional identity of [[lem-emg-maxwell-stress-divergence]], $\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^b{}_cj^c$, under its stated smoothness and source-sign hypotheses. For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on $\Omega$, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, define

$$J_\xi^a=(T_m^{ab}+T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab})\xi_b.$$

Then $\nabla_aJ_\xi^a=0$. If $C$ is a finite smooth singular $4$-chain in $\Omega$ with $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains, and $\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma\iota_{J_\xi}\mathrm{vol}_g$, then

$$\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-\mathcal Q_\xi(B).$$

In particular the two slice fluxes are equal when the side flux $\mathcal Q_\xi(B)$ vanishes.

There is also a local test-particle identity. Let $V\subseteq\Omega$ be open, let $A$ be a supplied smooth one-form on $V$ with $F=dA$, and let $\chi$ be a smooth scalar with $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\chi$. If $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is any interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and a $C^2$ curve $z:I\to V$ in the sense of clause (a) of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] has velocity $U=dz/d\tau$ (one-sided at included endpoints), $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and satisfies $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$ with the C$^2$-curve covariant acceleration of [[def-emg-c2-curve-covariant-acceleration]], for constants $m>0,q\in\mathbb R$, where $F^\sharp(U)^a=F^a{}_bU^b$, then

$$C=m g(U,\xi)+q\bigl(A(\xi)-\chi\bigr)$$

is constant along the curve. This is a conditional mathematical identity for a supplied field and an existing curve; it constructs no particle trajectory, global potential, Einstein solution, or point-source self-field.

items.title: Advected nonconstant charge ratio without Maxwell closure
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ with length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, future time-orientation $N=\partial_0$, and $x^0=ct$. In SI bookkeeping, assign $[\rho_0]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[L]=\mathrm m$, and $[\alpha_*]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$. Choose $\rho_0>0$, $L>0$, and $\alpha_*\ne0$. Set

$$U=c\,\partial_0,\qquad \rho=\rho_0,\qquad \alpha(x)=\alpha_*\left(1+(x^1/L)^2\right),\qquad \sigma=\rho_0\alpha,\qquad F=0.$$

The fields are smooth and the ratio $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$ is nonconstant in space. This is a mathematical example of the matter balance and transport equations; the sourced Maxwell equation is not imposed.

items.title: Explicit local conduction-energy calculation
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
On Minkowski space with length coordinates $x^0=ct$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and future time-orientation $N=\partial_0$, choose constants with SI units $[E_0]=\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$, and $[\epsilon_i]=[p_0]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, with $E_0\ne0$, $\chi>0$, $\epsilon_i>0$, and $p_0\in\mathbb R$. The open interval $I=(-\epsilon_i/(2\chi E_0^2),\epsilon_i/(2\chi E_0^2))$ has units of seconds; define

$$U=c\partial_0,\quad \mathbf E=E_0\mathbf e_x,\quad \mathbf B=0,\quad \epsilon(t)=\epsilon_i+\chi E_0^2t,\quad p=p_0,\quad \sigma=0,\quad q^a=(0,\chi E_0,0,0).$$

Let $F_{01}=-E_0/c$ with all other independent components zero, and set $j=q$. The interval ensures $\epsilon(t)>0$. The imposed field is a fixed background for the matter calculation; the nonzero current is not claimed to solve its Maxwell equation.

items.design_state: Complete example authored using only the separately proved test-particle clause of the A-page theorem; its item-level dependency closure still reaches the escalated Maxwell-stress supplier, so readiness remains escalated.
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $\phi\in C^\infty(\Omega,\mathbb R)$, assigned volts in SI bookkeeping. On $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\Omega$ with Minkowski metric, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, future time-orientation $N=\partial_0$, and length coordinate $x^0=ct$, take the static one-form $A=-(\phi/c)dx^0$ and $F=dA$. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $z:I\to M$ be an existing $C^2$ future-timelike curve parametrized by proper time $\tau$ in the sense of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]], with $U=dz/d\tau$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$ for constants $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$, assigned kilograms and coulombs respectively. Write $\mathbf w=d\mathbf x/dt$, $|\mathbf w|<c$, and $\gamma_L=(1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.
